model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (GAAP, not FTE). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026; FY0 = nine months 2026 actual 8,201 (NII 6,012 + noninterest income 2,189, Q3 2026 10-Q) + Q4 2026 at ~2,800 (NII ~2,075 on a NIM guided roughly flat at ~3.25%, fees ~725 after the Q3 step-down from 785 to 722). UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-29 build: Q3 revenue printed 2,791 against the 2,795/quarter assumed. Cross-check: guided ~35% NII growth on FY2025 5,991 = ~8,090 NII + ~2,915 fees = ~11,000. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027, the guidance year. The CSV `Revenue` column (FY2025 1,562; Q3 2026 484) is the ASC-606 fee subset tagged by XBRL and is NOT bank revenue; every revenue figure here is NII + noninterest income.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,015.4m common shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover, 2,015,387,251) PLUS ~27.6m dilutive awards (Q3 2026 diluted weighted average 2,046.9m less basic 2,019.3m) = ~2,043m fully diluted. No estimate is netted for unreported Q4 2026 repurchases (the >= $550m FY2026 programme leaves >= $141m, ~9m shares, for Q4); the 2026-09-29 build netted an estimated 10m for Q3 and the actual was 6.1m ($100m at $16.49), so the reported count is used as printed. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation ($148m in nine months) is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; the buyback is a distribution of the FCFE the model capitalises, not a separate driver.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. Huntington is a Fed/OCC-regulated bank holding company: long-term debt $17,341m and short-term borrowings $6,066m at 30 Sep 2026 and deposits $224,678m are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and due from banks $2,377m is held against that funding and is not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the ~10% CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only. Preferred stock ($2,881m, ~$164m/yr of dividends; $123m in nine months 2026) is a claim senior to common and is deducted at book in equity_bridge; the flows are therefore total net income (before preferred dividends), NOT net income to common, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = GAAP net income ~2,755 (nine months 2026 actual ~1,980 incl. $532m pre-tax of acquisition-related expense; Q4 at ~775 = (2,800 revenue - ~1,700 noninterest expense - ~150 provision) x (1 - 18.5%)) LESS capital retained ~800 (~4% organic RWA growth on ~$19bn tangible common equity). Cross-check on distributions: nine-month common dividends $877m + repurchases $409m; FY2026 ~$1,190m + >= $550m = ~$1.75bn, ~63% of GAAP NI, with CET1 at 10.1%. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 2,482; FY2022 4,027; Q3 2024 -58) is loan/deposit/trading movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV FreeCashFlow column is NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based compensation expense, Q3 2026 10-Q cash flow statement: $148m for nine months 2026 ($84m nine months 2025) -> ~$197m annualised on the post-Cadence headcount; FY2025 $130m, FY2024 $133m (CSV). ~1.8% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow. No separate net-share-settlement tax line; 'other share-based compensation activity' was -$69m in equity for nine months 2026 (shares withheld), immaterial to value.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: Repurchases of common stock $409m for nine months 2026 ($150m Q1, $159m Q2, $100m Q3 = 6.06m shares at $16.49); FY2026 programme >= $550m; management is seeking a $1.1-1.2bn authorisation for 2027. FY2022-FY2025 repurchases were nil. The flat share count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge in the flows; buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value. The FY2027 base FCFE (~$2.5bn) matches guided distributions: common dividends ~$1.25bn + preferred $164m + buybacks $1.1-1.2bn.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-09-30 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover count plus Q3 dilutive awards)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Huntington shareholders' equity $32,179m at 30 Sep 2026 less goodwill and other intangibles $10,393m (goodwill $9,527m) and preferred stock $2,881m = tangible common equity ~$18,905m = ~$9.38/share on 2,015.4m, DOWN from ~$9.55 at 30 Jun 2026: AOCI widened from -$2,213m to -$2,974m as rates rose, more than absorbing the quarter's retained earnings. TCE ratio 6.9% (7.1% at Q2), CET1 10.1% ($21,684m on RWA $214,442m). Reported ROTCE 14.6% in Q3 2026 and 13.8% for nine months, both depressed by acquisition-related expense ($117m in Q3, $532m year to date).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year US Treasury ~5.05% (Yahoo ^TNX at the valuation date, up from ~4.5% at the 2026-09-29 build) + beta 1.2 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = ~11.0%. RAISED from 10.5% solely because the risk-free anchor moved ~55bp; beta and ERP are unchanged. The same rate move is what widened AOCI by $761m in Q3, so the balance sheet and the discount rate now reflect the same yield curve. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, integration and deposit-cost risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium. If the 10-year returns to ~4.5% the rate reverts to 10.5% and the weighted value rises ~$1.2/share (see reconciliation).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branch network) are immaterial relative to $32.2bn of equity; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests (~$3m/quarter of income). Preferred stock is the only senior equity claim and is deducted at liquidation value in equity_bridge (see funding_note), so the 18.5% cash-tax-rate driver is pure income tax (FY2025 effective 17.1%; nine months 2026 18.5%; Q3 2026 19.3%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (house precedent NAB.AX, IAG.AX, GL) - UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-29 build. SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent, and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. BVPS-compounding is NOT used: GAAP book value is one-third goodwill after Cadence and swings with AOCI. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income (GAAP); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision for credit losses) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue; sbc_pct_path = 1.8%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation and core-deposit-intangible amortisation are inside noninterest expense and are genuine costs for a bank); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the ~10% CET1 target = NPAT margin x organic growth / return on tangible equity; cash_tax_rate_path = 18.5% income tax; wacc = cost of equity 11.0%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = -2,881 preferred stock. Q3 2026 ACTUALS the update rests on: revenue 2,791; noninterest expense 1,772 incl. 117 acquisition-related and 49 intangible amortisation (ex-acquisition GAAP efficiency 59.3%); provision 123 = 4.4% of revenue against net charge-offs of ~31bp (~147), i.e. a reserve release while nonperforming assets doubled year on year to $1.72bn; pre-tax 896 (1,013 ex-acquisition costs = 36.3% of revenue); tax 19.3%. Annualised ex-acquisition Q3 earnings are ~$1.54/share against FY2027 guidance of $1.75-1.83, so the guidance needs ~4 points of efficiency improvement from the Q3 run-rate. FY2027 base reconciliation: 11,000 x 1.05 = 11,550 revenue x (39.2% - 1.8%) x (1 - 18.5%) = 3,521 GAAP net income, less ~164 preferred dividends = 3,357 to common = ~$1.64 on the flat 2,043m count, ~$1.68 on the ~1,995m average count the guided $1.1-1.2bn buyback implies - below the bottom of the $1.75-1.83 range (which excludes notable items). That is a deliberate haircut: management has cut 2027 targets twice in 2026 and the Q3 cost base is not yet where the guidance needs it. Base FY2027 return on tangible common equity ~17.4% GAAP on ~$19.3bn average TCE, inside the lowered 17-18% target. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(CoE - g) = (17.4 - 2.5)/(11.0 - 2.5) = 1.75x x $9.38 = ~$16.4/share, which the engine base approximates; the market pays ~1.59x TBV. Price is the NASDAQ regular close at inputs.price_as_of, not an after-hours print. 30 Sep 2026 is the latest balance sheet (Q3 2026 10-Q).

equity_bridge.note: Preferred stock $2,881m at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q balance sheet, unchanged from 30 Jun 2026); dividends $123m for nine months 2026, ~$164m/yr. Deducted at book because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: UNCHANGED (annual series; FY2026 is not yet complete). For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (already after share-based compensation): FY2020 817 (COVID CECL build); FY2021 1,295 (TCF merger costs); FY2022 2,238; FY2023 1,951; FY2024 1,940; FY2025 2,211. The 5-year CAGR (22.0%) measures recovery from the FY2020 provisioning trough plus the TCF acquisition; the 3-year CAGR (-0.4%) is from the FY2022 NIM peak. Revenue = NII + noninterest income: FY2015 2,990; FY2020 4,815; FY2022 7,254; FY2025 8,166 (5-year 11.1% is TCF-inflated; underlying organic ~4-5%). Diluted EPS FY2020 0.69, FY2022 1.45, FY2025 1.39.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (5.0% FY27 tapering to 2.5%), anchored on the 3-year revenue CAGR (4.0%) which is the only organic window: FY2020-21 includes TCF, FY2025-26 includes Veritex and Cadence. Equity CAGRs (11-13%) are acquisition share issuance, not retained earnings.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3/5-year CAGRs (11.1%/13.4%) diverge >30% from revenue (4.0% 3-yr) and EPS (-1.4% 3-yr): book value grew through stock-funded acquisitions (TCF 2021, Veritex/Cadence 2025-26) and AOCI swings, not through compounding, so equity CAGR does not describe per-share earnings power. EPS 3-year is negative because FY2022 was the NIM peak and 2023-24 carried deposit repricing; the 5-year 15.0% is from the FY2020 trough. Growth is taken from the revenue series and the FY2027 guidance.

base.growth_rationale: Total revenue. FY27 CUT 5.5% -> 5.0%: the prior build credited an exit-2026 NIM in the mid/high-320s; management now guides Q4 2026 roughly flat at ~3.25% on a 50-60% deposit beta, and fees fell 8% quarter on quarter in Q3. Build: Q4 2026 run-rate (NII ~2,075 + fees ~725) x 4 = 11,200 is already +1.8% on FY0 because Q1 2026 held only two months of Cadence; plus ~3.5% NII growth from mid-single-digit average loans at a flat margin and ~3% fees = ~11,570. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED (4.5% tapering to 2.5%): nothing in Q3 speaks to organic growth beyond 2027; a second year of organic loan growth below ~4% or NIM below 3.20% would move them.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue. FY27 CUT from 38.4% to 37.4% pre-tax (39.2 with SBC 1.8): GAAP efficiency 56.6% (was 56.1%; Q3 2026 ran 59.3% ex-acquisition costs, so the guided mid/low-54% core exit rate is not yet visible and is given partial credit) and provision 6.0% (was 5.5%; ~32bp of net charge-offs on ~$197bn of loans plus a growth build - Q3 charge-offs were 31bp, the upper half of the 25-35bp guide, while the Q3 provision of 123 under-ran charge-offs and nonperforming assets doubled to $1.72bn, so the reserve release cannot repeat). FY28 38.1% and FY29 38.6% pre-tax: the synergy landing is pushed out about a year. MATURE pre-tax margin UNCHANGED at 38.8% from FY30 (efficiency 55.0%, provision 6.0% = ~33bp mid-cycle); the printed 40.6 vs the prior 40.5 is only the SBC add-back moving from 1.7 to 1.8. Evidence that would move the mature level: core efficiency still above ~56% after the FY2026 exit, or charge-offs sustained above 35bp.
base.capex_rationale: UNCHANGED. Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~10% as RWA grows = NPAT margin x organic balance-sheet growth / ROTE = ~1.95 x g. FY27-28 at 4.5% RWA growth: 8.8% of revenue (~$1.0bn, ~29% of NPAT retained). The new evidence corroborates rather than moves it: FY2027 FCFE of ~$2.5bn equals guided distributions (dividends ~$1.25bn + preferred $164m + the $1.1-1.2bn buyback authorisation sought), and 4.5% growth on $21.7bn of CET1 capital needs ~$0.98bn. Would move on a Category III capital requirement that brings AOCI (-$2,974m) into regulatory capital, or CET1 below 10%.
base.tax_rationale: RAISED 18.0% -> 18.5%, all years: nine-month 2026 effective rate 18.5%, Q3 19.3%, on the enlarged post-Cadence earnings base (FY2025 was 17.1%).

bull.growth_rationale: FY27 CUT 7.0% -> 6.5% for the same flat-NIM exit rate; the bull still needs NIM to drift up toward ~3.30% through 2027 as deposit betas settle, loans to grow 7-8% in Texas and the Southeast, and fees to resume ~8% growth. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED.
bull.margin_rationale: Pre-tax path UNCHANGED (40.0% FY27 -> 42.5% from FY30: GAAP efficiency 54.5% falling to 52.5%, provision 5.5% falling to 5.0%); each entry is +0.1 only for the SBC add-back moving to 1.8. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$1.79 on the flat count, the upper half of the $1.75-1.83 guidance; requires the full synergy plan to land from a Q3 2026 ex-acquisition efficiency of 59.3%.
bull.capex_rationale: UNCHANGED. Retention = NPAT margin ~34.9% x g / ROTE ~19.5% = ~1.79 x g: higher growth needs more capital even at a better return.

bear.growth_rationale: UNCHANGED. Deposit betas keep rising under a hiking Fed, NIM compresses toward ~3.05% and loan growth stalls at 1-2%. The Q3 NIM uptick to 3.25% and the flat Q4 guide neither confirm nor refute it.
bear.margin_rationale: Pre-tax path UNCHANGED (33.3% FY27, 30.8% FY28 credit cycle, 34.0% thereafter: efficiency ~58%, provision 8.5% -> 11.0% -> 8.0% of revenue, i.e. ~48bp -> ~62bp -> ~45bp); each entry is +0.1 only for the SBC add-back. Q3 2026 makes the path more plausible, not more severe: nonperforming assets doubled to $1.72bn and charge-offs reached 31bp, but that is what a ~48bp FY27 already assumes. Sustained charge-offs above 45bp in 2027 would deepen it.
bear.capex_rationale: UNCHANGED. Retention held at 5.5% in FY27-29 despite low growth because RWA migration and reserve build in a downturn consume capital (CET1 10.1%, TCE 6.9%).

scenario_narratives.base: Huntington digests Cadence and Veritex about a year slower than management guides. NIM holds ~3.25%, revenue grows 5% in FY2027 fading to 2.5%, efficiency improves from the Q3 2026 ex-acquisition 59% to ~56.6% in FY2027 and 55% by FY2030, and provisions run ~6% of revenue (~32-33bp) as the Q3 reserve release reverses. GAAP EPS is ~$1.64-1.68 in FY2027, below the reaffirmed $1.75-1.83, with ROTCE ~17.4% inside the lowered 17-18% target; roughly 70-85% of earnings are distributed, consistent with the $1.1-1.2bn 2027 buyback. At an 11.0% cost of equity the franchise is worth ~1.75x tangible book against the ~1.6x the market pays.
scenario_narratives.bull: Integration lands on plan, positive operating leverage takes efficiency to ~52.5% by FY2030, deposit betas settle so NIM drifts back toward ~3.30%, and the Texas/Southeast franchises grow loans 7-8% with credit benign at ~27bp. FY2027 EPS reaches the upper half of guidance and ROTCE ~19-20% exceeds the lowered target; repurchases scale up.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 guidance cuts are not the last. Deposit costs keep rising under a hiking Fed, NIM compresses toward 3.05%, loan growth stalls at 1-2%, and the doubling of nonperforming assets seen in Q3 2026 turns into a mid-sized credit cycle (CRE, the less-seasoned Texas/Southeast commercial book, vehicle finance) with provisions ~60bp in FY2028. Efficiency stays near 58%, ROTCE settles at ~12% (barely above the cost of equity) and the buyback is halted to rebuild a 10.1% CET1 with a 6.9% TCE ratio.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25 (house default 15/50/35). The Q3 2026 evidence cuts both ways and nets to no change: against - the ROTCE target was lowered to 17-18%, nonperforming assets doubled to $1.72bn, charge-offs are in the upper half of guidance, fees fell 8% quarter on quarter and TCE slipped to 6.9%; for - the FY2027 EPS range was reaffirmed rather than cut a third time, NIM ticked up to 3.25%, systems conversions are complete and a $1.1-1.2bn 2027 buyback is being sought. The credit and efficiency evidence is charged in the base FY2027-29 flows instead of the weights. Bear would go to 30% on Q4 charge-offs above 35bp or a third guidance cut; bull back toward 35% on two quarters of core efficiency at or below ~55% with stable nonperformers.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regional bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity - never on statutory operating cash flow (which is loan and deposit movement) and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. GAAP net income is the flow; capital retention at NPAT x g/ROTE is the reinvestment; preferred stock is deducted at book so the common claim is valued; 11.0% is the return an owner requires from a NIM-geared US super-regional with the 10-year Treasury near 5%. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a ~17.4% GAAP return on tangible common equity and 2.5% growth the franchise is worth ~1.75x tangible book, so the ~1.6x the market pays embeds either a ROTCE near 16% or a cost of equity near 12%. Most of the change since September is the discount rate, not the business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: the cost of equity moved 10.5% -> 11.0% with the 10-year Treasury and took ~$1.2/share off the weighted value; each 50bp is ~7%
Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$255bn of average earning assets is ~$130m of NII (~1.1% of revenue, ~3.5% of NPAT); management now models a 50-60% deposit beta against ~45% last cycle
Credit cycle: every 10bp on the provision rate over ~$191bn of loans is ~$190m pre-tax (~5% of NPAT); nonperforming assets doubled year on year to $1.72bn and Q3 2026 provisions under-ran charge-offs
Integration: FY2027 guidance needs ~4 points of efficiency improvement from the Q3 2026 ex-acquisition run-rate; the base credits ~2.7 points; every 1pp is ~$115m pre-tax (~2.6% of NPAT)

Capital: CET1 10.1% and TCE 6.9% leave little room; Category III status (average assets above $250bn from Q4 2026, after a transition period) or a credit cycle could force retention above the modelled g/ROTE and shrink the 2027 buyback
Share count: Q4 2026 repurchases (>= $141m, ~9m shares) are not netted; each 20m shares is ~1% of value per share
